title: Prototype capacity-aware steering + latency/geo pinning routing policy
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: design and validate a combined routing policy that uses latency-based routing, optional geo-pinning, and real-time capacity-aware steering to meet regional SLOs and minimize cross-region tail latency and cost. This ticket covers: prototype routing decision service, local simulator harness, experiment in staging + one canary region, and an incident/playbook for fallback behavior. Scope intentionally excludes UI to configure all knobs (to be tracked in PM-442).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Prototype router service deployed to staging with pluggable decision strategies (latency-based, geo-pin, capacity-aware).
2) End-to-end tests showing p95 request latency in synthetic multi-region workload <= 200ms for pinned traffic and <= 250ms for non-pinned in baseline config.
3) Circuit-breaker behavior verified in chaos test: when a region reports high error rate or capacity saturation the router correctly shifts >=50% of new traffic off the region within 15s.
4) Load-shedding behavior exercised with progressive degradation (reject vs queue vs soft-fallback) and documented metrics; integration test with Redwood load balancer.
5) Rollout plan and rollback criteria documented and sign-off from SRE and PM.
implementation_notes:
Design components:
- Router decision API (stateless): receives per-request metadata (region hint, customer pin, request type) and returns target region/variant and route_policy_id.
- Local capacity tracker: aggregates region-reported signals (available_slots, avg_cpu, queue_ms, error_rate) and computes capacity_score.
- Steering algorithm: score = w_lat*lat_norm + w_cap*(1 - cap_score) + w_cost*cost_norm; support hard geo-pin override.
- Circuit breaker: open when (error_rate > 0.5% && error_increase > 300% over 1m) OR (avg_queue_ms > 500ms) OR (cpu_95 > 90%). Auto-recover with half-open probes every 10s.
- Load shedding modes: soft-fallback -> reduce model size/quantized variant; reject with 429; queue with upper bound and client retry-after header.
- Telemetry: emit decision_reason, capacity_score, last_rebalance_ts, and metric tags for customer_id, model, route_id.

Trade-offs considered:
- Strong geo-pin reduces cross-region latency but lowers headroom for global capacity steering; decided to make geo-pin opt-in per-customer and fall back to soft-pin when capacity_score < threshold.
- Weight choices (w_lat vs w_cap) tuned in simulator; initial weights set to prioritize latency for interactive requests and capacity for batch/embedding workloads.
- Complexity vs observability: prefer simpler score with clear signals rather than opaque ML model for now.
simulation_results:
Staging simulator (multi-region traces from prod-week-sample) results:
- Baseline (no steering): p95 global = 310ms, cross-region failover rate during region outage = 18%.
- Latency+Capacity steering prototype: p95 global = 185ms, cross-region failover rate reduced to 6%.
- With geo-pin strict (no override): pinned customer p95 = 120ms, but global p95 increases for overflow periods by ~12% and capacity imbalance observed.
- Load shedding policy (soft-fallback to small-quant model) kept successful request rate > 92% under 2x load spikes vs 76% for reject-only approach.
monitoring_and_metrics:
SLOs targeted:
- Regional p95 latency target: <= 200ms for interactive generation (chat/generation).
- Regional error rate target: <= 0.2% (5xx).
- Availability SLO: 99.95% across regions for hosted tier.
Metrics to dashboard: per-region p50/p95/p99, per-region capacity_score, decision_counts(by reason), circuit_breaker_state, shed_count(by mode), cross-region-traffic-ratio, cost_delta_by-routing.
Alerting: Page when region capacity_score < 0.2 AND request_error_rate > 0.5% for 2m; Page on rollbacks during canary above threshold.
rollout_plan:
1) Feature-flagged deploy to staging (router & tracker) - smoke tests (3d).
2) Canary: enable routing for 5% traffic in a low-risk customer cohort in us-west-2 (48h). Monitor metrics; automatic rollback if p95 or error rate regression >10% relative to baseline for 15m.
3) Ramp to 25% in us-west-2 + enable soft geo-pin for 10 high-value customers (72h).
4) Open to additional regions in waves, each wave with 72h observation and SRE sign-off.
5) After 2 region waves and ops playbook validated, release runtime-1.22 with config exposed to PM console.

Rollback criteria: sustained p95 increase > 15% for 30m OR new 5xx rate > 0.5% absolute increase OR customer reported SEV impacting functionality.
security_considerations: Router receives customer region hints and customer_id; ensure no sensitive payload flows through decision path. Decisions computed from aggregated numeric signals only. KMS usage: decision logs encrypted at rest; ensure access control to decision logs. Security review requested only if we add customer-provided routing policies (tracked separately).

2026-02-20 - SRE review (R. Gomez): suggested lowering circuit-breaker probe interval to 10s and adding half-open probe limits. Implemented in prototype.
2026-03-02 - Infra review (K. Singh): flagged that capacity_score aggregation adds 40ms median to decision loop when using synchronous calls; changed to asynchronous pull with 50ms local caching.
2026-03-08 - Design review (M. Alvarez): recommended more explicit decision_reason labels for observability. Added reason taxonomy: latency, capacity, geo_pin, emergency_failover, manual_override.
testing_notes:
Test matrix:
- Unit tests for score normalization and circuit-breaker transitions.
- Integration test with load-balancer (simulate region outage, increase error rate, simulate CPU saturation).
- Chaos test: kill 2/3 replicas in one region and validate router shifts traffic according to policy within 15s window.
- Load test: 5x synthetic peak traffic to validate shedding and fallback model path.

Known limitations: the prototype uses a single capacity_score scalar; it may mask per-model bottlenecks. Future work (ENG-13101) will add model-level capacity signals.
